recipes.name: Make-Ahead Slow Cooker Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Combine flour, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, seasoned salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper in a large, resealable plastic bag. Add beef, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Shake bag until beef thoroughly coated with seasoned flour.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Remove beef from seasoned flour and shake off excess. Add beef, onion, and mushrooms to the skillet; cook and stir until beef is evenly browned and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease.

Transfer beef mixture to a slow cooker. Stir in carrots, potatoes, beef broth, celery, tomatoes, Marsala wine, onion soup mix, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, and remaining 1 teaspoon smoked paprika. Cover slow cooker.
Cook on High for 4 to 6 hours or on Low for 10 to 12 hours. Season with salt and black pepper.
Combine cornstarch and water in a small bowl; gradually stir into stew until thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Make-Ahead Slow Cooker Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: This hearty make-ahead slow cooker beef stew recipe can also be made fresh by browning the meat and then tossing all the ingredients in the slow cooker.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to put together a slow-cooker meal that has beef, mushrooms, potatoes, carrots, celery and lots of spices. This ultimate comfort food stew also freezes well. You'll be glad to have individual servings in your freezer for last-minute suppers.

review.reviewBody: This was so good! My search for a great beef stew is finally over. My husband raved about it while he was eating it, mentioned it again later that night, and then raved again when we had leftovers the next night. I cooked the beef stew on low overnight and had my husband shut it off when he got up so it would cool enough for me to put it in the refrigerator before I left for work. It was so good I couldn't stop taking bites. That night, I let it simmer on the stove for about an hour while I made some corn bread to go with it and I had all I could do not to take a bowl. But I convinced myself to wait until I thickened it and it was so worth it. I made no changes to the recipe other than not putting in the mushrooms (my husband hates them) and I used regular paprika and diced tomatoes since that is what I had. I had never put tomatoes in a beef stew but I really think it added something. Thanks for sharing.

Doubled it. Already had the meat cooked so I didn't do step 1 & 2 other than fry the onions. Any red wine should do. I had IKEA's Glogg, a mulled wine, that I had on hand. I needed a bigger pot than my crock pot so I cooked it on the stove in my extra large dutch oven. I simmered it for about 4 hours. Everything was perfect!

I have finally found a beef stew recipe that everyone loves. I don’t use the onion soup mix because this recipe doesn’t need artificial enhancement. I substitute 1 T salt and 1 T dried onion. I also use red wine instead of Marsala because I don’t want to buy a whole bottle just for 1/4 cup. I deglaze the skillet with the wine to cook off the alcohol and grab the yummy remnants. If you like extra broth use a lg can of crushed tomatoes. I did that by accident the first time and it was yummy.

This was delicious! Everyone devoured and leftovers went quickly. Only slight modifications- I listened to other reviewers and cut the beef broth in half which turned out perfectly. Instead of Marsala, I used the red blend I had on hand and omitted the mushrooms. I used baby brown potatoes, halved with skin on and to save time on prep, I browned the meat the night before and then cooked on low for 12 hours the following day. Smelled delicious when returning home from work! Will definitely make again.

This is very good. I make two batches ahead and freeze for easy weeknight dinners. I do not freeze the liquid ingredients as mentioned in chef’s notes- I just cook the beef with the garlic and freeze the meat and veggies separately. When ready to cook- I let the veggies and meat thaw and then add the broth, tomatoes, marsala and onion mix after I put the meat and veggies in my crockpot. It’s best to cook for at least 12 hours. I add frozen peas for the last 30 minutes.

Very easy and delicious! I doubled the recipe and used an Instant Pot. Here are my changes:
I set the Instant Pot for Stew for 10 hours
With 4 lbs of beef and all the veggies I could only fit in 4 cans of broth instead of the suggested 6. I was originally worried about this and thought it would reduce too much but with the Instant Pot it ended up being almost too much liquid! If you do make it on a stove or a traditional Crock Pot that might not be the case. I couldn't even fit the tomatoes in with everything but I wasn't happy about putting them in anyways and it doesn't need them! It would have made the stew too sour and acidic in my opinion. Also, I used Cabernet instead of Marsala and it was perfect. Marsala is too sweet to me. The only other thing I did differently is added parsley at the end. I will definitely be making this again, it was a huge hit!

As usual, I used a couple of recipes.
for seasoning, i used McCormick Stew seasoning, 1 pkt. Added 2T of Worcestershire, 3t of minced garlic, 1tsp smoked Paprika
mixed it all in 2- 14.5 oz cans beef broth, and 14.5 oz stewed tomatoes w juice, and 8 oz Red wine
veggies incl: 4 potatoes, 6 celery, 6 carrots, 2 onions, , 2- 4oz cn mushrooms, 1-15oz can corn

It turned out wonderful and tastes a lot like Dinty Moore Beef Stew. I made some minor adjustments. I cooked the potatoes separately to prevent over cooking them. I only used one carrot finely sliced and cooked separately. I also omitted the Celery because we were having a snow storm and Celery was not worth a trip to the store! I used a can of Hunt's Diced Tomatoes which were already seasoned with Basil, Garlic and Oregano instead of the Tomato Paste. I used 3.5 pound of Stew meat and 16 ounces of whole white Mushrooms which I pre-steamed prior to adding to the Crock Pot so my ingredients would fit nicely. And I used regular Paprika. I see Recipes as a guide and work with what I have on hand.

First time I made it I found there was insufficient vegetables for the amount of beef and gravy. Second time I doubled the potatoes & carrots and used 3 sticks of celery. I also added to the vegetables 2 yellow onions - quartered. This is a great stew.

Made this today; delicious. My changes: no mushrooms or wine (didn't have any and couldn't shop); used fire roasted diced tomatoes; used double amount of Worcestershire. This was a perfect "comfort food" to eat during the current pandemic quarantine. As the recipe suggested, I did the cornstarch slurry and it was suitably thick. I also made E Z Drop Biscuits (recipe on this site), which were excellent go-withs.

The best stew I ever made and I’m 80! Changes were 1 pound of meat, no mushrooms, 2 cups of beef broth, red wine, can of diced tomatoes and only 1t of paprika. I used the leftover seasoned flour to make the gravy. I cooked it on low for 8 hours. Savory and delicious.
very easy with good results

This is an excellent recipe. I did food prep in the evening and put everything in slow cooker bag in the crock and refrigerated until morning then let it slow cook while I was at work. I added 3 strips chopped fat rendered bacon, fresh thyme, sage and rosemary and used an extra teaspoon of the smoked paprika in the flour mix. Also added some wine at the end of the beef browing process.
I was out of mushrooms, and I braised the beef before adding the rest of the ingredients. P.S. In an airpot, try 35 minutes on high pressure, and a natural release will work out good as well!!!
This was delicious. I didn't have mushrooms or the French Onion soup mix but it still was very good.
I really liked it added a tablespoon of garlic and red pepper to spice it up. I would definitely make this again.

I thought it took a bit of work and a number of ingredients to get it started but, once everything was in the crockpot I turned it on low and let it set for seven 7 1/2 hours and the house smelled amazing when I got home. Very good. I added extra veggies, including peas, green beans, and corn because I like a lot of veggies. Good comfort food on a cold night! TY
Great flavor

I've made this recipe exactly as is over the past several years and my husband and I love it. I am actually making it tonight for dinner and my house smells so good. Can't wait for it to be done. Delicious!

Delicious. Love the crockpot! Now, I need to try it with the smoked paprika. I need to buy some. I’m sure it will be more pleasant flavor. I did thicken it with cornstarch. I think that’s key for this “stew”.
